=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:46-64 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The Bash renderer strips leading indentation before matching placeholders and emits replacement blocks without re-indenting them, so indented prompt templates are rendered incorrectly.
  WHY: All three reviewers identified the same regression in the replacement path; x-ai notes it affects every Codex invocation that routes through render_prompt.sh.
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:66-80 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The unresolved-placeholder checks only look for the trimmed placeholder text, so indented placeholders can survive rendering without tripping the failure path.
  WHY: This is a separate edge case from the replacement-path indentation bug and can produce a malformed prompt instead of the intended early exit.
- scripts/workspace_safety_check.sh:25-44 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Path.resolve(strict=False) followed by relative_to() does not fully prevent symlink or bind-mount escapes from the intended workspace root.
  WHY: Both reviewers note that a workspace path can canonicalize into the allowed prefix while still escaping the runner's real workspace boundary, defeating the exit-78 safety contract.
- scripts/memory_helpers.sh:434-end | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The _memory_force_tick_* helper block was deleted, breaking callers that still source or guard for those functions and changing orchestrator behavior.
  WHY: Reviewers agree the removal is an unrelated backward-compatibility break; it can silently alter force-tick persistence and dispatch behavior even if some callers use declare -F guards.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- File: scripts/render_prompt.sh
  Line or code reference: lines 48-64 (the while/read + case block)
  Problem: The trimmed_line logic strips leading whitespace from every input line before pattern-matching against stripped placeholder names, then emits the replacement block with no re-indentation.
  Why it fails at runtime: No current prompt template places these tags with leading whitespace — all instances in `prompts/mode-*.txt` sit at column 0 — so the bug is latent today. However, the Bash rewrite drops the indentation-preserving contract that the Python implementation maintained, and a future template that indents any of the three tags will silently corrupt the rendered prompt.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/memory_helpers.sh
  Line or code reference: removed functions _memory_force_tick_remote_url, _memory_force_tick_remote_branch_exists, _memory_force_tick_ensure_branch, _memory_force_tick_collision_wrapper, memory_force_tick_get, memory_force_tick_put (413 lines, lines 434-end of previous version)
  Problem: These six functions were deleted in the same commit that delivers W3 workspace safety. They are still sourced and reference-checked by `scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh` via `declare -F` guards, so callers degrade gracefully — no runtime crash. However, the removal is entirely unrelated to workspace safety invariants and violates the issue's own guardrail "Keep this issue about safety invariants only. Do not fold in thread reuse or overlay behavior."
  Why it fails at runtime: No immediate runtime failure because callers use existence guards, but the loss of force-tick state persistence changes orchestrator behavior invisibly — tick deduplication and cooldown state no longer persist across poll cycles, so the orchestrator may double-dispatch force ticks.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- Requirement: "Invoke it before each Codex launch in the listed implement/validate/review/conflict paths."
  Expected change site: scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh line 77
  Evidence of absence: The safety check is invoked via `bash "${WORKSPACE_SAFETY_CHECK_HELPER}"` with no preceding `[ -f ... ]` or `[ -x ... ]` existence check. All other scripts that invoke a helper variable guard against absence (e.g., `[ -x "${CODEX_STALL_GUARD_HELPER}" ]`). If `WORKSPACE_SAFETY_CHECK_HELPER` points to a missing file due to a bootstrap failure, the editor will exit with a bare "No such file or directory" error rather than the intended `workspace_safety_violation / exit 78` message. The issue asks for the invocation to fail with the contract error code on safety violations; a bootstrap gap that short-circuits to a different failure mode is a completeness gap on the safety-invariant contract.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
- File: scripts/workspace_safety_check.sh
  Line or code reference: lines 25-44 (resolve_workspace_path function)
  Problem: Path traversal check uses Path.resolve(strict=False) which follows symlinks, potentially allowing workspace escape
  Why it fails at runtime: An attacker-controlled WORKSPACE_PATH symlink pointing outside the runner_temp workspaces directory would be followed by resolve(), passing the relative_to check while the actual working directory escapes the intended boundary
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/render_prompt.sh
  Line or code reference: lines 46-64 (while IFS= read loop and case statement)
  Problem: Placeholder replacement strips original indentation from template lines
  Why it fails at runtime: When a placeholder like `    {{SERENA_TOOL_HINTS}}` appears indented in a prompt template, the replacement block is printed without that leading whitespace, corrupting YAML/markdown structure in the rendered prompt sent to Codex
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: scripts/render_prompt.sh
  Line or code reference: lines 46-64
  Problem: The case statement matches trimmed_line (whitespace-stripped) but prints replacement text without re-applying the captured indentation
  Why it fails at runtime: Multi-line replacement blocks lose their structural relationship to surrounding template content, breaking semantic formatting
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: scripts/memory_helpers.sh
  Line or code reference: lines 434-846 (removed functions)
  Problem: Removal of memory_force_tick_get and memory_force_tick_put functions breaks backward compatibility
  Why it fails at runtime: These functions are called by scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh (which sources memory_helpers.sh). While the caller may have declare -F guards, removing 413 lines of functional code unrelated to the W3 workspace safety scope is an unjustified breaking change
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- Requirement: "Add `scripts/workspace_safety_check.sh`. Invoke it before each Codex launch in the listed implement/validate/review/conflict paths."
  Expected change site: scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh (reviewer Codex launches), review_reject_verify.sh, summariser path, plus complete bootstrap lists in both implement.yml and review_autofix.yml
  Evidence of absence: LAST RUN DIFF / PR DIFF added the script + three call sites + one check_required_file, updated the implement.yml bootstrap list, but review_run_reviewers.sh (the main reviewer launch path), review_reject_verify.sh, the summariser path, and the reviewer bootstrap list in review_autofix.yml:4798 remain untouched. The test only asserts wiring in 5/6 launchers.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- Requirement: "Tests cover both violations and the gated no-op path."
  Expected change site: tests/test_workspace_safety_check.py (full contract test for safety_check + render_prompt.sh semantics).
  Evidence of absence: The test only exercises four rejection / no-op cases. There is no test confirming that the new Bash renderer produces identical output to the old Python path for complex templates (with all three placeholders at varying indentation levels), nor any test that actually runs render_prompt.sh against a real prompt template. The wiring test only checks string presence, not semantic equivalence of rendered output.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- Requirement: "Keep this issue about safety invariants only. Do not fold in thread reuse or overlay behavior."
  Expected change site: scripts/memory_helpers.sh
  Evidence of absence: The commit also performed a large unrelated cleanup: wholesale deletion of 413 lines of memory_force_tick helpers from memory_helpers.sh and a full rewrite of render_prompt.sh that removes the Python delegation. These changes exceed the guardrails and should have been a separate PR.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
- File: scripts/workspace_safety_check.sh
  Line or code reference: resolve_workspace_path() Python heredoc (lines 25-44)
  Problem: Path.resolve(strict=False) + relative_to() does not fully canonicalize against the runner’s real workspace layout (overlayfs, bind mounts, symlinks).
